git init -q . && git config user.name e2e && git config user.email e2e@lap
"$LAP" init >/dev/null 2>&1 # no .gitignore of the project's own: lap's guards .lap
"$LAP" commit "$f" --no-session -i "seed the fixture" -b "records $f as the base" >/dev/null 2>&1
git ls-files .lap | grep -qv '^\.lap/\(\.gitignore\|log/\)' && fail "git tracks more of .lap than log/"
printf 'F\n' > f.txt && "$LAP" commit f.txt --branch b -i "change f in b" -b "rewrites f.txt in b" >/dev/null 2>&1

old_text: **A shared history can be corrupted by merging it.** If `.lap/log/` is
tracked by git and two git branches of one folder both record commits,
merging them conflicts on the chunk both appended to, and resolving that by
interleaving lines breaks the hash chain. `lap verify` will detect the
damage (naming a sealed chunk that changed) but cannot repair it. Either
keep recorded history on one line of work, or add `.lap/` to `.gitignore`
